lesson_title: Four Thousand Settlers on a Beach
hook_text: In 1820, about four thousand British people waded ashore at Algoa Bay, promised a hundred acres each. It didn't go as planned.
clip_script: Britain, 1819: wars are over, jobs are gone. The government offers poor families free passage to the Cape and a hundred acres. About four thousand are chosen. They land at Algoa Bay in 1820, where the town of Port Elizabeth, now Gqeberha, begins. Ox wagons carry them to the Zuurveld, land the Xhosa had been driven from only eight years before. Crops fail, floods come, and many settlers move to town to trade instead. Grahamstown's forts, Khoikhoi soldiers and British magistrates watch over a frontier that is about to get even tenser.
visual_style: Boats landing on a wide beach with families and luggage; ox wagons heading inland; a fort on a hill above a small town.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson on soldiers, officials and British immigration.
